paths.description: Homepage/news portal entry point and navigation; tested default, dark, reduced-motion/high-contrast, mobile, no-JS, network, performance, memory, privacy and security conditions.
Representative NewsArticle content template, including metadata and non-JavaScript discoverability.
Representative sport section/listing template at a narrow viewport.
Scores/results utility, representing a primary interactive information-finding journey.
Live match surface, representing frequently updating content and status communication.
Synthetic missing URL used to inspect HTTP failure and recovery behaviour.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot remains a white consent surface, and the platform probe found no prefers-color-scheme, light-dark(), or color-scheme implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface, text and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: Motion continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found two running 1500 ms animations while the platform probe found no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential motion in a no-preference query and provide a reduced or static state.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not explicitly supported.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no forced-colors or prefers-contrast CSS, while Lighthouse also found ordinary color-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations and retain visible native control boundaries.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no declarative transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS across the loaded styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance meaningful route/state changes with same-document or cross-document View Transitions, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures the entire site on every audited first-visit path.
findings.evidence: Homepage, article, results and live screenshots all show a full-screen blurred backdrop and consent panel before content can be used.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a compact, non-obscuring consent surface and keep reject/accept choices immediately available.

findings.summary: The consent modal is custom role-based UI rather than the native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence found one [role=dialog] but no <dialog>; the panel uses custom fixed-position chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with correct modal focus handling and declarative close behaviour.

findings.summary: Dense navigation, score strips, category bars, advertising slots and side rails compete with editorial content.
findings.evidence: The full-page homepage screenshot shows repeated chrome and ad placeholders across an 11,895 px page, with content cards occupying a minority of several sections.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary navigation and ad chrome, and prioritise the current section’s editorial hierarchy.

findings.summary: The mobile experience is a scaled desktop canvas rather than a responsive layout.
findings.evidence: The viewport meta is width=970; a requested 360 px viewport produced a 989 px layout viewport scaled to 0.364, and section/article probes reported 972 px scroll width against 780 CSS px inner width.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and fluid intrinsic layouts; remove the fixed 970 px viewport contract.

findings.summary: Reusable components do not use component-level responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no @container rules; narrow captures retain desktop-density cards and navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable score, card and sidebar components, with viewport queries only for page-level composition.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and many controls are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focused Zaloguj link computed to outline none/0 px; 64 of 475 visible controls measured below 24 px in at least one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide strong :focus-visible styles and enlarge interactive hit areas to at least WCAG target-size expectations.

findings.summary: First-visit core journeys are blocked behind a consent decision with rejection hidden in advanced settings.
findings.evidence: Results and live-page screenshots expose only “Ustawienia zaawansowane” and a prominent accept action; the requested content cannot be used until this detour is completed.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow core reading and score lookup without consent to optional processing, with an immediate reject-all action.

findings.summary: The 404 response does not present an explicit error or recovery state.
findings.evidence: The URL returned HTTP 404, but the rendered DOM had no h1 and reused the homepage title/content behind the consent wall, with no “not found” explanation or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a dedicated 404 heading, explanation, search and links back to current sections while retaining the 404 status.

findings.summary: The lab mobile load misses the LCP performance target.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.7 s, FCP 3.9 s, TTI 7.5 s and performance 0.64; the trace’s unthrottled LCP was 1.64 s, showing network/CPU conditions expose the problem.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, shorten render-blocking chains and defer non-critical script and consent/marketing work.

findings.summary: Resource delivery includes render blockers and weak cache/font behaviour.
findings.evidence: HAR found a parser-blocking stylesheet and synchronous head script plus a 529 KB uncached PNG; Lighthouse estimated 410 ms render-blocking, 440 KiB cache and 120 ms font-display savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, inline only critical CSS, set durable immutable caching and use non-blocking font-display with stable fallbacks.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused and legacy JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 292 KiB unused JavaScript and 15 KiB legacy JavaScript; HAR recorded 36 scripts and 605 KB transferred script bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by template and interaction, remove legacy transforms for modern targets and conditionally load marketing features.

findings.summary: Some foreground/background combinations fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust affected foreground and background tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state, including consent and navigation UI.

findings.summary: Heading sequence and focus visibility are not reliable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; the homepage h1 is empty and the explicit focus probe found no visible outline on the focused login link.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each template one meaningful h1, repair heading levels, and add persistent :focus-visible treatment in DOM reading order.

findings.summary: The fixed viewport prevents genuine reflow and leaves controls too small.
findings.evidence: The page declares width=970 rather than device width; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport and the probe counted 64 controls below 24 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a device-width viewport, preserve pinch zoom, reflow content at 320 CSS px and increase target sizes.

findings.summary: Image asset presentation has quality and sizing defects.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image aspect-ratio and responsive-resolution audits and partially failed explicit dimensions; image inspection found 60/100 without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide correct intrinsic dimensions/aspect-ratio and responsive srcset/sizes variants at the rendered aspect ratio.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable and the viewport is not mobile friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and meta-viewport; the live DOM otherwise had many real href links and robots allowed normal indexing.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real destination href values for all navigation and switch to a device-width viewport.

findings.summary: Baseline transport defenses and cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but header inspection found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie inspection found 13 insecure cookies and widespread SameSite=None, including 390–400 day identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark cookies Secure and use the least-permissive SameSite/lifetime.

findings.summary: The first-visit data/third-party footprint is disproportionate.
findings.evidence: The consent copy names 1,017 IAB plus 846 other partners; network evidence saw 12 third-party origins, 69/91 requests and 957 KB third-party bytes, including Salesmanago and Survicate.
findings.suggestedFix: Block optional vendors before consent, minimise partner scope and identifiers, and batch only necessary analytics.

findings.summary: Installability exists, but no offline cache/fallback was evident.
findings.evidence: A manifest and active service-worker registration exist, but the controlled-page probe was false and Cache Storage had no keys after load.
findings.suggestedFix: Precache a lightweight offline shell and current/previous articles, then provide explicit stale/offline messaging and retry.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling is misleading.
findings.evidence: A real 404 response renders homepage-like content with no not-found heading or explicit recovery controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Create intentional 404/5xx/offline templates with accurate status, clear state, search, retry and section links.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually and procedurally asymmetric.
findings.evidence: The consent wall gives a large green “Akceptuję” action while rejection is hidden behind “Ustawienia zaawansowane”; copy proposes sharing identifiers with 1,863 partner entries.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent accept-all and reject-all actions, granular optional choices, and no access penalty for refusal.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently resolution-efficient.
findings.evidence: HAR’s largest asset is a 529 KB PNG; Lighthouse estimates 109 KiB image savings and image inspection found 60/100 images without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, use srcset/sizes and avoid oversized decorative PNGs.

findings.summary: Third-party script cost is high relative to the core reading task.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 69/91 requests and 957 KB of 1.61 MB transferred; multiple marketing/survey origins load before a consent decision.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and defer optional marketing, survey and personalisation code until explicit consent or interaction.

findings.summary: The homepage has a large initial memory/DOM footprint.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 508,411 nodes and 31.0 MB self size for a news listing. Repeated-scroll capture stayed similar, but the one-state footprint is disproportionate.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise/defer deep offscreen sections, release hidden ad/consent trees and use content-visibility for below-fold content.

taskList.title: Make consent non-blocking, symmetric and privacy-minimised
Replace the fixed 970px mobile canvas with device-width responsive layouts
Harden security headers and cookie attributes
Improve LCP and trim render-blocking/unused JavaScript
Repair keyboard focus, heading order and color contrast
Add preference-driven dark, reduced-motion and high-contrast modes
Reduce third-party and image transfer budgets
Provide intentional 404 and offline recovery states
Reduce page chrome and initial DOM/memory footprint
Correct image aspect ratio, responsive sizing and crawlable links
Use native dialog and progressive View Transitions
